entry.title: Germs of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of the line at zero are torsion-free
entry.statement:
Every finite subgroup of the group $\operatorname{Diff}^+_0(\mathbb R,0)$ of
germs at $0$ of orientation-preserving local diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb R$
fixing $0$ is trivial: if $h$ is such a germ and $h^n=\mathrm{id}$ in the group
of germs for some $n\ge1$, then $h=\mathrm{id}$. Equivalently, the group of
germs of orientation-preserving local diffeomorphisms fixing a point of a
one-dimensional manifold is torsion-free.
entry.strategy: Fix a positive integer $n$ and suppose $h^n$ is the identity germ. Choose an increasing representative $h$ near $0$; shrink a neighborhood so all its first $n$ iterates are defined there and $h^n(t)=t$. If $h$ were not the identity germ, there would be arbitrarily small $t$ on one of the two sides of $0$ with $h(t)\ne t$. If $h(t)>t$, monotonicity gives $h^{k+1}(t)>h^k(t)$ for every $k<n$; if $h(t)<t$, the inequalities are reversed. Either case contradicts $h^n(t)=t$. Thus every finite-order germ is identity, and each element of a finite subgroup has finite order, so the subgroup is trivial. The argument requires only finite restrictions and no choice principle.

entry.title: A co-oriented closed transversal detects nonvanishing rational homology of a compact leaf
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a
transversely oriented smooth codimension-one foliation of a closed oriented
$n$-manifold $M$, $n\ge2$. Orient a closed immersed transversal $\gamma$ and
orient every compact hypersurface leaf $S$ by the ambient orientation together
with the positive transverse normal. Then:

1. the intersection count $I(\gamma,S)$ has one sign and is nonzero whenever
   $\gamma$ meets $S$;
2. $I(\gamma,S)$ depends only on the rational homology classes
   $[\gamma]\in H_1(M;\mathbb Q)$ and $[S]\in H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb Q)$;
3. if $\gamma$ misses compact leaves $S_1,\dots,S_k$ but meets the compact leaf
   $S$, then $[S]$ lies outside the rational span of
   $[S_1],\dots,[S_k]$ in $H_{n-1}(M;\mathbb Q)$;
4. the same conclusions hold for a finite union of compact leaves carrying
   these consistent orientations.
entry.strategy: Transversality and compactness make intersections finite; the induced leaf orientation and positive direction of γ give the same local determinant sign at every point. Homology invariance is a finite-chain argument, not merely homotopy invariance. Smooth any specified finite rational bounding chain compatibly on faces by the declared relative simplex-smoothing supplier; clear denominators first if needed. Use finite smooth perturbations, compatible on common faces, transverse to the fixed smooth immersed γ, preserving its given transverse boundary intersections. Pulling back γ on each n-simplex gives a compact oriented one-dimensional inverse-image chain. Its boundary points on common simplex faces cancel with the rational coefficients, while the remaining boundary is exactly the intersection chain of γ with the bounding hypersurface cycle. Every finite oriented interval has total signed boundary zero; subdividing the compact one-dimensional inverse images into finitely many arcs therefore proves I(γ,∂C)=0. The same argument applies to changing the closed γ by a finite bounding chain. No perturbation is claimed to remove prescribed boundary intersections. Bilinearity now proves nonvanishing and the span conclusion by evaluating a hypothetical linear relation against γ. All choices are finite for the specified cycles/chain; the standing ACω suffices. Finite immersed transversal self-crossings do not change this argument, which uses its parametrization.

entry.title: Mapping torus foliations realize global Reeb stable examples
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $L$ be a nonempty connected closed
smooth manifold and $f:L\to L$ a diffeomorphism
([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]). Let $\mathbb Z$
act on $L\times\mathbb R$ by $n\cdot(x,t):=(f^n(x),t+n)$ and let
$M:=(L\times\mathbb R)/\mathbb Z$ be the associated **mapping torus**. Then:

1. $M$ is a closed smooth manifold;
2. the product foliation of $L\times\mathbb R$ by the slices $L\times\{t\}$ is
   invariant under the action and descends to a codimension-one regular
   foliation $F_f$ of $M$ whose leaves are the images of the slices;
3. every leaf of $F_f$ is compact and diffeomorphic to $L$, with trivial
   holonomy;
4. the projection $(x,t)\mapsto t\bmod 1$ descends to a smooth map $M\to S^1$
   whose fibres are exactly the leaves, exhibiting $F_f$ as the fibre foliation
   of a locally trivial fibre bundle over $S^1$ with fibre $L$;
5. the suspension/base direction (the image of $\partial/\partial t$) is
   transverse to the fibres, and its first-return map on the fibre
   $L\times\{0\}$ is $f^{-1}$, the monodromy for this quotient convention.

The foliation has a compact leaf with trivial holonomy, and it realizes the circle-fibration conclusion directly. The finite-fundamental-group global theorem applies to this foliation when $L$ is connected with finite fundamental group. Bundles over $S^1$ with fibre $L$ are classified up to isomorphism by
the conjugacy class of the monodromy in $\pi_0\operatorname{Diff}(L)$; hence
this bundle is the trivial bundle $L\times S^1$ if and only if $f$ is isotopic
to the identity, and monodromies with nonconjugate classes in $\pi_0\operatorname{Diff}(L)$ realize distinct bundle structures over the fixed oriented base circle. No claim is made about $M$ as a bare manifold.
entry.strategy:
The $\mathbb Z$-action is free and properly discontinuous (the $t$-coordinates of its translates of a product neighbourhood are disjoint), i.e. a covering-space action, and it preserves the product foliation by the slices because $n\cdot(L\times\{t\})=L\times\{t+n\}$; [[prop-quotient-foliation-under-a-free-proper-foliated-action]] then provides the smooth structure on $M$ and the descended regular foliation. Leaves are the images of the slices $L\times\{t\}$, each diffeomorphic to $L$ and compact. Holonomy is trivial because the leafwise transport in the product $L\times\mathbb R$ is the identity and the quotient is taken by deck transformations acting leafwise. The map $(x,t)\mapsto t\bmod 1$ is invariant and descends; its fibres are the leaves, and over an interval of the base the product structure $L\times I$ trivializes it, which is local triviality. The vector field $\partial/\partial t$ is invariant and transverse; after one unit of its flow the point $(x,0)$ represents $(f^{-1}(x),0)$, so the first-return map is $f^{-1}$ for the displayed action convention. The classification of $L$-bundles over $S^1$ up to bundle isomorphism by conjugacy classes in $\pi_0\operatorname{Diff}(L)$ (equivalently: a bundle isomorphism over the identity of the base identifies the monodromies up to isotopy) gives the stated triviality criterion; only the bundle structure is classified, and no claim about $M$ as a bare manifold is made. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: The Reeb foliation of the solid torus has the boundary as a leaf
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let
$X:=\overline D^2\times S^1$ be the solid torus, where
$\overline D^2=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2\le1\}$
([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]) and $\partial X\cong S^1\times S^1$
is the boundary torus ([[def-two-dimensional-torus]]). Define
$u:\operatorname{Int}\overline D^2\to(0,\infty)$ by
$u(r):=\exp\bigl(1/(1-r^2)\bigr)$ for $0\le r<1$, with $r=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$, and
consider the level sets of the submersion $f(x,y,t)=u(r)-t$ on
$\operatorname{Int}\overline D^2\times\mathbb R$; add the boundary $\partial X$
as a leaf. This defines a codimension-one regular foliation
$F_{\mathrm{Reeb}}$ of $X$ tangent to $\partial X$
([[def-foliation-tangent-to-the-boundary-of-a-manifold-with-boundary]]), and:

1. the boundary $\partial X$ is a compact leaf diffeomorphic to $T^2$;
2. every other leaf is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2$ and accumulates on the
   boundary leaf;
3. the foliation is invariant under the translation $t\mapsto t+1$, so it
   descends to the quotient $X=\overline D^2\times\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$;
4. the holonomy group of the boundary leaf is infinite: the holonomy of the
   loop in the $S^1$-factor through a boundary point is represented by the germ
   of the contraction $r\mapsto r'$ determined by $u(r')=u(r)+1$, a
   non-identity germ of a one-sided interval; consequently the boundary leaf is
   compact but has infinite holonomy and is not stable
   ([[def-stable-leaf-of-a-foliation]]).
entry.strategy:
The function $f$ is a submersion on $\operatorname{Int}\overline D^2\times\mathbb R$ with nowhere-vanishing differential because $\partial_t f=-1$; its level sets are smooth surfaces of revolution, and [[cor-kernel-of-a-constant-rank-submersion-is-integrable]] integrates the kernel distribution, giving a regular codimension-one foliation of the open solid cylinder whose leaves are the level sets. Each level set is the graph of $t=u(r)-c$ over the punctured disk, hence diffeomorphic to the once-punctured disk times $S^1$, i.e. to $\mathbb R^2$; it accumulates on $\{r=1\}\cong T^2$ because $u(r)\to\infty$ and the spiral wraps infinitely often. Adding the boundary as a leaf is the boundary-tangency condition of [[def-foliation-tangent-to-the-boundary-of-a-manifold-with-boundary]]; a half-space chart at a boundary point is obtained from $(r,\theta,t)$ with $s=1-r\ge0$. The translation $t\mapsto t+1$ preserves the level sets, is a covering-space action on the open cylinder, and [[prop-quotient-foliation-under-a-free-proper-foliated-action]] descends the foliation to $X$; the quotient of the boundary circle is again a circle. The holonomy computation is the transport of a radial transversal through one turn of the $S^1$ factor: the leaf through $(r,\theta,0)$ reaches the same transversal at time $1$ at the unique $r'$ with $u(r')=u(r)+1$; since $u$ is strictly increasing this $r'$ satisfies $r'>r$ (the map is nontrivial), and $r'\to1$ as $r\to1$, so the germ is a one-sided contraction. Hence the holonomy group contains a non-identity element and is infinite, and stability fails by [[def-stable-leaf-of-a-foliation]]. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Transverse orientability is load-bearing in the global codimension-one form
entry.statement:
Assume the standing countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]); the following finite quotient construction needs no further choice. On $S^2\times S^1$, with $\theta\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, consider $\tau(x,\theta)=(-x,-\theta)$. This involution is free, because the antipodal map on $S^2$ has no fixed point. Small disjoint neighborhoods of a point and its image give smooth quotient charts, so $X=(S^2\times S^1)/\langle\tau\rangle$ is a closed connected smooth three-manifold.

The product foliation descends. For $\theta\ne0,1/2$ a pair of slices at $\theta,-\theta$ has image diffeomorphic to $S^2$. At $0$ and $1/2$ the slice is identified antipodally and its image is $\mathbb RP^2$. All these leaves are compact and have finite fundamental group. The leaf space is the quotient of the circle by reflection, hence a closed interval, with the two projective-plane leaves at its endpoints.

The descended foliation is not transversely orientable ([[def-transversely-oriented-codimension-one-foliation]]). Indeed a hypothetical nonzero coorientation would pull back to $a(x,\theta)\,d\theta$ on the connected product, where $a$ is a continuous nowhere-zero function. Invariance under $\tau$ requires $a(-x,-\theta)=-a(x,\theta)$, impossible because a continuous nowhere-zero real function on a connected space has constant sign. Thus the common-leaf and circle-fibration conclusions of global Reeb stability fail when transverse orientability is removed. Under full AC this is a counterexample to removing just that hypothesis from the global theorem, rather than an application of its proof under countable choice alone.
entry.strategy: The involution is free because $(-x,-\theta)=(x,\theta)$ would force $x=-x$ on $S^2$; the quotient is therefore a closed manifold. The foliation and its leaves are computed as in Mrowka, Remark 7: the image of a slice $S^2\times\{\theta\}$ is a sphere for generic $\theta$ and a projective plane for the two $\theta$-classes fixed by $\theta\mapsto-\theta$, and the normal bundle of the descended foliation is the quotient of the trivial co-orientation line by the $-1$ action of $\tau$, hence non-orientable. The failure of the global conclusion is therefore a genuine failure of the hypothesis, not of the proof. No choice principle beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

entry.title: Thurston stability: finitely generated groups of C¹ interval germs are locally indicable
entry.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial finitely generated subgroup of
$\operatorname{Diff}^{1,+}_0(\mathbb R)$, the group of germs at $0$ of $C^1$
orientation-preserving local diffeomorphisms of $\mathbb R$ fixing $0$
([[def-c1-germ-of-a-local-diffeomorphism-at-a-point]],
[[lem-c1-germs-of-local-diffeomorphisms-form-a-group]]). Then there is a
surjective homomorphism $G\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z$; that is,
$\operatorname{Diff}^{1,+}_0(\mathbb R)$ is locally indicable.
entry.strategy: The group operation is well defined by [[lem-c1-germs-of-local-diffeomorphisms-form-a-group]], and the $C^1$ local-diffeomorphism terminology is [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]], [[def-group]] and [[def-subgroup]]. Use the derivative homomorphism $d(g)=\log g'(0)$. If $d|_G$ is nonzero, its image is a nonzero finitely generated torsion-free abelian subgroup of $\mathbb R$; the classification of finitely generated abelian groups ([[cor-fundamental-theorem-of-finitely-generated-abelian-groups-from-pid-modules]]) makes it $\mathbb Z^r$ with $r\ge1$, and projection onto one factor gives a surjection to $\mathbb Z$. If $d|_G=0$, choose generators $g_1,\ldots,g_m$. Unless $G$ is trivial, some generator moves points arbitrarily close to $0$ on at least one side; work on that side and choose $x_n\to0$ with $w_n=\max_j|g_j(x_n)-x_n|>0$. The normalized displacement vectors $a_n=((g_j(x_n)-x_n)/w_n)_j$ lie in the compact cube $[-1,1]^m$ with maximum norm $1$; a convergent subsequence has limit $a$ with maximum norm $1$. Since $g_j'(0)=1$, $w_n=o(|x_n|)$. For each fixed word, induction over its letters shows each partial word moves $x_n$ by $O(w_n)$; continuity of the first derivatives makes the displacement of the next generator at that point differ from its displacement at $x_n$ by $o(w_n)$. The mean-value theorem first bounds inverse-letter displacement by $O(w_n)$ and then gives its normalized contribution as the negative generator coordinate. Thus every fixed word has normalized displacement converging to its signed exponent sum paired with $a$. A relation has identically zero displacement near $0$, so its limiting exponent sum is zero. The limit therefore defines a homomorphism $G\to\mathbb R$, nonzero because some coordinate of $a$ has absolute value $1$. Its image is a nonzero finitely generated torsion-free abelian group, hence has a quotient $\mathbb Z$. This expands the compressed estimates in Calegari's proof; only $C^1$ regularity, specifically continuity of the first derivative, is used.

entry.title: A compact C¹ leaf has finitely generated fundamental group
entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $L$ is a compact
connected leaf of a transversely oriented $C^1$ codimension-one foliation of a
smooth manifold, then $\pi_1(L,x)$ is finitely generated for every $x\in L$
([[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]).
entry.strategy: The compact leaf is an embedded C¹ hypersurface by [[lem-compact-c1-foliation-leaf-is-an-embedded-hypersurface]]. The transverse coordinates of foliation charts give local C¹ defining functions $f_i$ whose differentials along $L$ are positive multiples of the coorientation conormal; their chart neighborhoods cover $L$, so compactness gives a finite subcover. Choose smaller neighborhoods with closures inside these charts and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to them ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]). The weighted sum $f=\sum_i\chi_i f_i$, with supported terms extended by zero, is C¹ and vanishes on $L$. At each $p\in L$, its differential is $df_p=\sum_i\chi_i(p)d(f_i)_p$, a positive coorientation conormal because every active $d(f_i)_p$ is a positive multiple of that conormal; hence $df_p\ne0$. For each $p\in L$ such a positive local field exists on a neighborhood of $p$; these neighborhoods cover $L$. Compactness gives a finite subcover, and a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it combines the corresponding fields into a smooth vector field $V$ with $df(V)>0$ on $L$. Compactness gives $df(V)>c>0$ on a smaller neighborhood. The smooth flow exists there for a uniform time ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution]]). The map $(p,t)\mapsto\Phi_t(p)$ has invertible derivative at every $(p,0)$, since $T_pL\oplus\mathbb RV(p)=T_pM$; the C¹ inverse function theorem and compactness give a uniform flow collar after shrinking. For the global injectivity step, if no common time interval were injective, distinct $(p_j,t_j),(q_j,s_j)$ with $t_j,s_j\to0$ and equal images would have a subsequence converging to the same $(p,0)$, contradicting local injectivity there. Along each flow segment $f$ is strictly increasing from $0$, so this collar also shows $f^{-1}(0)=L$. Smooth $f$ in C¹ on a compact subcollar by a finite-chart mollifier argument: decompose it using a finite smooth partition, extend each supported coordinate function by zero to Euclidean space, convolve with a standard mollifier ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]]), and use uniform continuity of both the function and its first derivatives on the compact supports to obtain uniform convergence of the functions and their first derivatives. The finite sum is smooth and can be made arbitrarily C¹-close to $f$. Let $\widetilde f$ be close enough that $d\widetilde f(V)>c/2$ and its values at the two ends of each flow segment have opposite signs. The smooth flow of $V$ and monotonicity in the flow parameter give exactly one zero of $\widetilde f$ on each segment; the C¹ implicit function theorem ([[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]) makes that zero a C¹ function of the basepoint. Thus the nearby zero set is a smooth compact hypersurface homeomorphic to $L$ and is a regular level set ([[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]]). Apply [[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]] to this smooth zero set. A finite CW model has a finite connected $1$-skeleton, whose fundamental group is finitely generated; attaching its finitely many $2$-cells takes a quotient by [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]], and cells of dimension at least $3$ do not change $\pi_1$ because their attaching spheres are simply connected ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]). The homeomorphism transfers finite generation to $\pi_1(L,x)$ ([[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]). The finite-CW supplier uses full AC, and its countable-choice hypothesis is derived locally from AC by [[lem-axiom-of-choice-implies-countable-choice]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

entry.title: The rational homology of a closed smooth manifold is finite-dimensional in each degree
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]) and the Axiom of Choice
as consumed by [[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]
and [[lem-subgroups-of-free-abelian-groups-are-free]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Let $M$ be a closed smooth manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]],
[[def-compact-space]]). Then $H_k(M;\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated for every
$k$, and the rational vector space $H_k(M;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional. In
particular $H_2(M;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional, and every subspace of
$H_k(M;\mathbb Q)$ generated by countably many homology classes is
finite-dimensional.
entry.strategy:
By [[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]] $M$ has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex $X$, and a homotopy equivalence induces isomorphisms on homology with every coefficient group. Since $X$ has finitely many cells, its cellular chain groups are finitely generated and free over $\mathbb Z$, hence finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$ after tensoring, and [[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]] identifies $H_*(X;G)$ with the homology of the cellular complex with coefficients $G$ for every abelian group $G$. With $G=\mathbb Q$ this exhibits $H_k(M;\mathbb Q)$ as a quotient of a subspace of a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space, hence finite-dimensional. With $G=\mathbb Z$: the cycle group $Z_k$ is a subgroup of a finitely generated free abelian group, hence free and finitely generated ([[lem-subgroups-of-free-abelian-groups-are-free]]), the boundary group $B_k$ is a quotient of a finitely generated abelian group, hence finitely generated, and therefore $H_k(M;\mathbb Z)\cong Z_k/B_k$ is finitely generated. Finally a subspace of a finite-dimensional space that is spanned by countably many vectors is spanned by finitely many of them. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the axiom of choice used by [[lem-subgroups-of-free-abelian-groups-are-free]] and the choice consumed by [[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]] are used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Trivial C¹ holonomy gives a saturated product neighbourhood
entry.statement:
Let $F$ be a transversely oriented $C^1$ codimension-one foliation of a smooth
manifold $M$, and let $L$ be a compact leaf with trivial $C^1$ holonomy
([[lem-c1-holonomy-is-a-well-defined-representation-into-transverse-germs]]).
Then there are an open interval $D$ and a saturated open neighbourhood $U$ of
$L$ with a $C^1$ foliated diffeomorphism
$$(U,F|_U)\cong\bigl(L\times D,\ \{L\times\{t\}\}_{t\in D}\bigr),$$
that is, a $C^1$ diffeomorphism carrying the foliation $F|_U$ onto the product
foliation by the slices.
entry.strategy: Prove compact injectivity for a local C1 diffeomorphism equal to inclusion on the central slice. Normalize finitely many plaque-chart first integrals by actual positive path-transport representatives. Construct a smooth positively transverse field from finitely many chart bumps and a C1 flow collar. Trivial loop germs give equality of normalized first integrals on ambient neighborhoods of each overlap point; compact overlap closures and finitely many pairs give one actual common collar domain. The resulting global C1 first integral has positive collar derivative. Uniform endpoint bounds and the inverse function theorem construct Φ=(P,r)^-1 on L×D. Each slice is compact, open and closed in its intrinsic connected Hausdorff leaf, hence the full leaf; the image is saturated. All selections are finite, with no new AC hypothesis.

entry.title: Gluing two Reeb components gives a foliation of the three-sphere
entry.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $X_1,X_2$ be two
copies of the solid torus $\overline D^2\times S^1$ with their Reeb foliations
([[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]]) and let
$\sigma:\partial X_1\to\partial X_2$ be the diffeomorphism which interchanges
the two circle factors, written in the boundary coordinates
$\partial X_j\cong S^1\times S^1$ as $\sigma(u,v)=(v,u)$. Then the glued
manifold $X_1\cup_\sigma X_2$ is diffeomorphic to the three-sphere $S^3$
([[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]]), the standard genus-one splitting,
and the two Reeb foliations glue by
[[lem-gluing-manifolds-with-boundary-along-a-boundary-diffeomorphism]] to a
codimension-one regular foliation $F_{\mathrm{Reeb}}$ of $S^3$. This foliation
has exactly one compact leaf, the Heegaard torus
$\partial X_1=\partial X_2$
([[def-two-dimensional-torus]]), whose holonomy group is infinite; every other
leaf is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2$ and accumulates on the torus leaf. Hence
a compact manifold can carry a codimension-one foliation with non-compact
leaves and a single unstable compact leaf.
entry.strategy: Realize $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and write it as the union of the two closed solid tori $V_1=\{|z_1|^2\le\frac12\}$ and $V_2=\{|z_2|^2\le\frac12\}$ meeting along the torus $\{|z_1|=|z_2|=1/\sqrt2\}$. The maps $V_1\to\overline D^2\times S^1$, $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(\sqrt2\,z_1,z_2/|z_2|)$, and $V_2\to\overline D^2\times S^1$, $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(\sqrt2\,z_2,z_1/|z_1|)$, are diffeomorphisms (the second coordinate is well defined since the other coordinate is nonzero on each closed piece), and on the common boundary torus the transition is $(u,v)\mapsto(v,u)=\sigma$. Thus $S^3\cong X_1\cup_\sigma X_2$ with the stated gluing map, and the foliation claim is the gluing lemma applied to the Reeb foliations, which are tangent to the boundary with the boundary torus as a single leaf on each side, so the compatibility hypothesis of the gluing lemma holds automatically. The unique compact leaf and the accumulation behaviour are inherited from [[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]]; a non-compact leaf of the glued foliation lies in one of the two Reeb components, so it is a plane, and the torus leaf retains its infinite holonomy. The statement uses the standard description of the genus-one Heegaard splitting, which is proved here by the explicit formulas. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

entry.title: Reeb-Thurston stability for codimension-one leaves with vanishing first real cohomology
entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $F$ be a $C^1$
transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$, and
let $L$ be a compact leaf with $H^1(L;\mathbb R)=0$
([[def-singular-cohomology-with-coefficients]]). Then $L$ has a saturated open
neighbourhood whose leaves are all diffeomorphic to $L$. In fact the holonomy
of $L$ is trivial and the neighbourhood can be chosen to be a product foliated
neighbourhood $L\times D$ for an open interval $D$. This is the local
cohomological refinement; no global fibration conclusion is asserted.
entry.strategy: Assume AC and fix $x\in L$. By [[lem-compact-c1-leaf-has-finitely-generated-fundamental-group]], $\pi_1(L,x)$ is finitely generated. Apply the degree-one Hurewicz theorem and the cohomological universal-coefficient sequence to the singular chain and cochain complexes ([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]], [[def-singular-cochain-complex-with-coefficients]], [[def-singular-cohomology-with-coefficients]], [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]). Since $L$ is connected, $H_0(L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ ([[prop-zero-th-singular-homology-is-free-on-path-components]]); this free module is projective ([[thm-free-modules-are-projective-with-choice-boundary]]), so the Ext term in degree one vanishes. Hence $H^1(L;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_1(L,x),\mathbb R)$, and the hypothesis makes every real character trivial. By [[lem-c1-holonomy-is-a-well-defined-representation-into-transverse-germs]], the holonomy image is a finitely generated subgroup of orientation-preserving C¹ interval germs. If it were nontrivial, [[thm-thurston-stability-for-c1-interval-germ-groups-are-locally-indicable]] would give a surjection of that image onto $\mathbb Z$; composing with holonomy and $\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$ would yield a nonzero real character of $\pi_1(L,x)$, a contradiction. Holonomy is therefore trivial, and [[lem-trivial-c1-holonomy-gives-a-saturated-product-neighbourhood]] gives the saturated product neighbourhood and diffeomorphic leaves. AC is used by the published universal-coefficient and finite-CW suppliers and is declared in the statement.

entry.title: Finite holonomy acts on a small transverse disk
entry.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation, $L$ a leaf, $x\in L$, and $T$ a local transversal to $F$ at $x$
chosen to be an embedded open disk
([[def-local-transversal-to-a-regular-foliation]]). Suppose
$H=\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)\le\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$ is finite
([[def-holonomy-representation-and-holonomy-group-of-a-leaf]]). Then there is
an $H$-invariant open neighbourhood $D\subseteq T$ of $x$ such that:

1. every $h\in H$ has a representative diffeomorphism defined on $D$ with
   $h(D)=D$, and these representatives make $H$ act on $D$ by diffeomorphisms
   restricting the given germs;
2. each $h\in H$ extends to a diffeomorphism defined on a neighbourhood of the
   closure of $D$;
3. if in addition the finitely many germs preserve a metric germ on $T$, the
   disk $D$ may be taken to be an open metric ball.

Any open $H$-invariant $D$ suffices for the finite-holonomy normal model.
entry.strategy:
Since $H$ is finite, first choose representatives and restrict their domains so every finitely many group-law equality $g\circ h=gh$ holds on one neighborhood, and all representative images of a smaller neighborhood lie inside every composition domain. Then choose representatives $h:U_h\to T$ of the finitely many elements of $H$ and of their inverses on a common open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ (a finite intersection of neighbourhoods). The finite intersection $D_0:=\bigcap_{h\in H}h(U)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$, and for $g\in H$ one has $g(D_0)=\bigcap_{h\in H}gh(U)=\bigcap_{k\in H}k(U)=D_0$ because $gH=H$; moreover each $g|_{D_0}$ is a diffeomorphism of $D_0$ restricting the given germ. For (ii), choose the common domain $U$ relatively compact in $T$; then $D$ can be shrunk so that the closure of $D$ is still contained in $U$, whence each representative extends to a neighbourhood of the closure. For (iii), if the germs preserve a metric germ, average the metric over the finite group to obtain an invariant metric germ and take a small metric ball. The germ group structure supplies the compatibility of representatives on overlaps. The construction is finite and uses only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: The deck group of the holonomy cover is the holonomy group
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation, $L$ a leaf, $x\in L$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$,
$\rho_x:\pi_1(L,x)\to\operatorname{Diff}_x(T)$ the holonomy representation and
$p:\widehat L\to L$ the holonomy cover, with $\hat x\in p^{-1}(x)$ and
$p_*\pi_1(\widehat L,\hat x)=\ker\rho_x$
([[def-holonomy-cover-of-a-leaf]]). Then:

1. $p$ is a regular covering, $\pi_1(L,x)/\ker\rho_x$ acts faithfully on
   $\widehat L$ by deck transformations, and
   $\operatorname{Deck}(p)\cong\pi_1(L,x)/\ker\rho_x\cong\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)=\rho_x(\pi_1(L,x))$;
2. the deck action is a covering-space action,
   $\widehat L/\operatorname{Deck}(p)\cong L$, and the quotient map is $p$;
3. the holonomy group acts through transverse germs via $\rho_x$; when those
   germs are realized on a common invariant transverse neighbourhood $D$, the
   diagonal action of $H=\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)$ on $\widehat L\times D$ is
   free and a covering-space action. In particular, when $H$ is finite, $p$ is
   a finite-sheeted covering of degree $|H|$.
entry.strategy: Use the path-class construction of the holonomy cover with $N=\ker\rho_x$: a point over $y$ is represented by a path $a$ from $x$ to $y$, with representatives identified when the resulting based loop lies in $N$. For a based loop $\gamma$ at $x$, prepend $\gamma$ to $a$; normality of $N$ makes this independent of both representatives. On lifted simply connected plaque neighborhoods this is a smooth deck map, and prepending $\gamma^{-1}$ is its inverse. Traversal-order concatenation gives $\tau_\gamma\tau_\delta=\tau_{\gamma*\delta}$, so the kernel is $N$ and the action on each fibre is transitive and free. Uniqueness of lifts shows every deck map is obtained this way. Thus $\operatorname{Deck}(p)\cong\pi_1(L,x)/N\cong\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)$, and the covering-space-action lemma gives the quotient $\widehat L/\operatorname{Deck}(p)\cong L$. Holonomy elements initially act as transverse germs; when $H$ is finite, the next lemma realizes them on one invariant neighborhood $D$. The diagonal action there is free and a covering-space action because the first factor is one. Its fibres have $|H|$ points. Each deck map is defined on path classes, without selecting a representative for every class; only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ foliation interface is used.

entry.title: The finite-holonomy normal model of a compact leaf
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation, $L$ a compact leaf, $x\in L$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$ that is
an embedded disk ([[def-local-transversal-to-a-regular-foliation]]),
$H=\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)$ a finite holonomy group,
$D\subseteq T$ an $H$-invariant open disk-like neighbourhood as in
[[lem-finite-holonomy-acts-on-a-small-transverse-disk]], and
$p:\widehat L\to L$ the holonomy cover with
$\operatorname{Deck}(p)\cong H$ acting by the covering-space action of
[[lem-deck-group-of-the-holonomy-cover-is-the-holonomy-group]]
([[def-holonomy-cover-of-a-leaf]]).

The **finite-holonomy normal model** of $(L,T,D,H)$ is the quotient
$$\mathcal N:=\bigl(\widehat L\times D\bigr)\big/ H,\qquad h\cdot(\hat y,t):=(h\,\hat y,\,h\,t),$$
with the diagonal $H$-action given by the deck action on $\widehat L$ and the
holonomy action on $D$, together with the foliation $\mathcal F_{\mathcal N}$
obtained from the product foliation of $\widehat L\times D$ by the slices
$\widehat L\times\{t\}$, which the diagonal action permutes. The quotient is a
smooth foliated manifold: the diagonal action is free and a covering-space
action and preserves the product foliation, so
[[prop-quotient-foliation-under-a-free-proper-foliated-action]] applies; the
product carries its canonical product smooth structure
([[prop-products-of-smooth-manifolds-have-a-canonical-product-smooth-structure]]),
and the diagonal formula defines an action of the finite group $H$
([[def-group-action]]).

The **central leaf** of the model is the image of $\widehat L\times\{x\}$; it
is canonically diffeomorphic to $L$, because $\widehat L/H\cong L$ by the
deck-group lemma and $x$ is fixed by the holonomy action. The leaves of
$\mathcal F_{\mathcal N}$ are the images of the slices $\widehat L\times\{t\}$;
the holonomy group of such a leaf is the finite stabilizer $H_t\le H$ of $t$,
and the slice $\widehat L\times\{t\}$ finitely covers its image because $H_t$
is finite. Every leaf of the model other than the central one is therefore
finitely covered by the holonomy cover of $L$, and all leaves of the model are
compact when $L$ is. The model realises $F$ near $L$ in the sense that the
central leaf is $L$ and the local foliation near it is the one induced by the
product foliation of $\widehat L\times D$; the descent to $F$ itself is proved
in the normal-model map lemmas below.
entry.strategy:
Apply the quotient-foliation proposition to the finite group $H$ acting diagonally on $\widehat L\times D$: the deck action is a covering-space action and $D$ is $H$-invariant, so the diagonal action is a covering-space action (a product of a covering-space action on $\widehat L$ and a finite action on $D$) and preserves the product foliation by the slices $\widehat L\times\{t\}$ because $h\cdot(\widehat L\times\{t\})=\widehat L\times\{ht\}$. The quotient therefore carries a smooth structure and an induced regular foliation of the same codimension. The central leaf is $(\widehat L\times\{x\})/H\cong\widehat L/H\cong L$ by the deck-group lemma. Holonomy of the model's leaves is computed from the stabilizer $H_t$ in the finite action on $D$, hence is finite; the covering $\widehat L\times\{t\}\to(\widehat L\times\{t\})/H_t$ is finite since $H_t$ is finite. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Transverse holonomy transport is well defined and equivariant on the model
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation, $L$ a compact leaf, $x\in L$, $T$ a local transversal at $x$ that is
an embedded disk, $D\subseteq T$ an $H$-invariant open neighbourhood, and
$p:\widehat L\to L$ the holonomy cover. Then there is a well-defined smooth map
$$\Phi:\widehat L\times D\longrightarrow M,\qquad \Phi(\hat y,t)=\text{endpoint of the leafwise transport of }t\text{ along a path representing }\hat y,$$
with the following properties: (i) $\Phi(\hat y,t)$ lies in the leaf through
the initial transverse point $t$ and is obtained by a transverse transport map
defined on $D$ along a leafwise path from $x$ to $p(\hat y)$; (ii) $\Phi$ is
well defined, independently of the choice of path representing $\hat y$ and of
the auxiliary foliation chart chain, by chain independence and homotopy
invariance of the holonomy germ; (iii) $\Phi$ is invariant under the diagonal
action of $H$, $\Phi(h\cdot\hat y,h\cdot t)=\Phi(\hat y,t)$ for every $h\in H$,
where $H$ acts on $\widehat L$ by the deck action and on $D$ by the holonomy
action; consequently $\Phi$ descends to the model quotient
$(\widehat L\times D)/H$; (iv) $\Phi|_{\widehat L\times\{x\}}=p$; (v) $D$ may be
shrunk so that all finitely many chart transitions involved are defined on $D$,
uniformly over $\widehat L$, because $L$ is compact and the germ family is
$H$-equivariant.
entry.strategy:
Cover the compact leaf $L$ by finitely many foliation charts and choose the invariant transverse neighbourhood $D$ so small that, in each chart of the covering, the plaque transports are defined on $D$; compactness of $L$ (= compactness of the finite cover and of the finitely many transition maps involved) makes this uniform. For $\hat y$ represented by a leafwise path $a$ from $x$ to $p(\hat y)$, set $\Phi(\hat y,t):=h_a(t)$, the plaque transport of [[lem-a-leafwise-path-determines-a-germ-of-transverse-diffeomorphism]] transported along $a$. Chain independence and homotopy invariance make this independent of the representative of $\hat y$. Invariance: fix $h\in H$ and a loop $\gamma$ at $x$ with $\rho_x([\gamma])=h$, and let $\hat y$ be represented by a path $a$ from $x$ to $p(\hat y)$; with the left deck action convention $h\cdot\hat y:=\tau_{h^{-1}}(\hat y)$ of [[lem-deck-group-of-the-holonomy-cover-is-the-holonomy-group]], the point $h\cdot\hat y$ is represented by the concatenation of $\gamma^{-1}$ with $a$, and transport along that concatenation is $h_a\circ\rho_x([\gamma])^{-1}$, so $\Phi(h\cdot\hat y,h\cdot t)=h_a(h^{-1}ht)=h_a(t)=\Phi(\hat y,t)$; the diagonal quotient identification then makes $\Phi$ descend to the model. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: The normal model map is a foliated local diffeomorphism
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). In the situation of
[[lem-transverse-holonomy-transport-is-well-defined-and-equivariant]], the map
$\Phi$ is $H$-equivariant, so it descends to a smooth map
$$\overline\Phi:\mathcal N=(\widehat L\times D)/H\longrightarrow M,\qquad \overline\Phi\bigl([(\hat y,t)]\bigr):=\Phi(\hat y,t).$$
Then: (i) $\overline\Phi$ maps leaves of the model foliation into leaves of
$F$; (ii) $\overline\Phi$ is a local diffeomorphism; (iii) the differential of
$\overline\Phi$ is invertible at every point of the central leaf and induces
the canonical identification of the central leaf with $L$; (iv) $\overline\Phi$
is a foliated local diffeomorphism, carrying the model foliation locally onto
$F$.
entry.strategy:
Well-definedness and smoothness of $\overline\Phi$ follow from equivariance and the quotient description of $\mathcal N$. On the central leaf $\widehat L\times\{x\}$ the map is $p$, a covering hence a local diffeomorphism in the leaf direction; in the transverse direction the differential at $(\hat y,x)$ is the differential of the transport germ $t\mapsto\Phi(\hat y,t)$, which is an invertible germ by [[lem-finite-holonomy-acts-on-a-small-transverse-disk]] and the definition of the holonomy transport as a germ of local diffeomorphism. The two directions span the tangent space because the plaques and the transversal are transverse; hence $d\overline\Phi$ is invertible at central points, and by continuity and local invariance it remains invertible on a neighbourhood of the central leaf; on the rest of the model the same argument applies leafwise with the transport germs. Leaves are mapped into leaves because each $\Phi(\cdot,t)$ is obtained by plaque transport inside leaves. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: The normal model map restricts to a diffeomorphism onto a saturated neighbourhood
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). In the situation of
the two preceding lemmas there is an $H$-invariant open neighbourhood
$D'\subseteq D$ of $x$ such that the descended map
$\overline\Phi:(\widehat L\times D')/H\to M$ is injective. Consequently
$\overline\Phi$ is a foliated diffeomorphism of the model
$(\widehat L\times D')/H$ onto a saturated open neighbourhood
$U=\overline\Phi\bigl((\widehat L\times D')/H\bigr)$ of $L$, and every leaf of
$F|_U$ is compact with finite holonomy and is finitely covered by the holonomy
cover $\widehat L$. The neighbourhood $U$ can be taken inside any prescribed
neighbourhood of $L$.
entry.strategy:
$\overline\Phi$ is a local diffeomorphism mapping the central leaf onto $L$; since $L$ is compact, cover $L$ by finitely many foliation charts with relatively compact plaques, and use the induced product structure to show that a small invariant $D'$ makes $\overline\Phi$ injective. Explicitly: if $\overline\Phi([(\hat y_1,t_1)])=\overline\Phi([(\hat y_2,t_2)])$ with $t_i$ in a sufficiently small invariant neighbourhood of $x$, then the two points lie in a common plaque-transport chart of the finite cover, and chain independence together with the $H$-equivariance identifies $[(\hat y_1,t_1)]=[(\hat y_2,t_2)]$ in the model. Compactness of $L$ (through the finite chart cover and the finite group $H$) supplies a uniform size. An injective local diffeomorphism from the manifold $\mathcal N$ onto $M$ is a diffeomorphism onto its image, which is open and saturated because the model foliation maps leaf to leaf. Shrinking $D'$ puts $U$ inside any prescribed neighbourhood of $L$. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Local Reeb stability for compact leaves with finite holonomy
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation of a smooth manifold $M$ and let $L$ be a compact leaf whose holonomy
group is finite. Then $L$ is stable ([[def-stable-leaf-of-a-foliation]]): for
every open neighbourhood $W$ of $L$ there is a saturated neighbourhood
$U\subseteq W$ of $L$ and a foliated diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open
neighbourhood of the central leaf in the finite-holonomy normal model
$(\widehat L\times D)/H$ of [[def-finite-holonomy-normal-model]], carrying $L$
to the central leaf. Moreover, after shrinking, the neighbourhood $U$ admits a
retraction $\pi:U\to L$ such that for every leaf $L'\subseteq U$ the restriction
$\pi|_{L'}:L'\to L$ is a finite covering and $\pi^{-1}(y)$ is a transverse disk
for every $y\in L$; every leaf of $F|_U$ is compact with finite holonomy group
and is finitely covered by the holonomy cover $\widehat L$. The hypothesis
consumed is finiteness of the holonomy group, not finiteness of $\pi_1(L)$; no
orientability of $F$ or $M$ is required.
entry.strategy:
Choose a transversal disk $T$ at a point $x\in L$, shrink it to an $H$-invariant disk $D$ as in [[lem-finite-holonomy-acts-on-a-small-transverse-disk]], build the finite-holonomy normal model, and form the model map $\overline\Phi$; the preceding lemmas show that $\overline\Phi$ restricts to a foliated diffeomorphism of a neighbourhood of the central leaf onto a saturated neighbourhood of $L$, inside any prescribed $W$. Compactness of $L$ and finiteness of $H$ are used only to obtain the uniform transverse size and the finite covering description. The retraction is induced by the projection of the model to $D$ composed with the identification of the central leaf with $L$; fibres are the $H$-orbits of the deck action, and leaf intersections are finite coverings by the deck-group lemma. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Trivial holonomy gives a product foliated neighbourhood
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation and $L$ a compact leaf whose holonomy representation is trivial
(equivalently, whose holonomy group is the trivial group)
([[def-holonomy-representation-and-holonomy-group-of-a-leaf]]). Then the
finite-holonomy normal model with $H=\{1\}$ is $\widehat L\times D$ with
$\widehat L=L$, and $L$ has arbitrarily small saturated neighbourhoods $U$
foliated-diffeomorphic to products $L\times D$ with the product foliation by
the slices $L\times\{t\}$. In particular every leaf of $F|_U$ is compact and
diffeomorphic to $L$, and $L$ has a fundamental system of product foliated
neighbourhoods.
entry.strategy:
When $\rho_x$ is trivial, $\ker\rho_x=\pi_1(L,x)$, so the holonomy cover of [[def-holonomy-cover-of-a-leaf]] has $\pi_1(\widehat L)=\pi_1(L)$ and is the identity cover: $\widehat L=L$; the deck group is trivial and the model is the product $L\times D$ with the product foliation. Local Reeb stability then gives the saturated neighbourhood foliated-diffeomorphically to a neighbourhood of the central leaf $L\times\{x\}$, i.e. to some $L\times D'$ by shrinking $D$. Product neighbourhoods of the form $L\times D'$ with $D'\subseteq D$ form a fundamental system. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: Finiteness of the fundamental group is sufficient, but not necessary, for Reeb stability
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair, lem-images-of-finitely-generated-and-finite-groups-are-finitely-generated-and-finite]]). Let $F$ be a regular
foliation and $L$ a compact leaf. If $\pi_1(L,x)$ is finite then the holonomy
group $\operatorname{Hol}(L,x)=\rho_x(\pi_1(L,x))$, being a homomorphic image
of a finite group, is finite; hence $L$ is stable by
[[thm-local-reeb-stability]]. Finiteness of $\pi_1(L)$ is therefore sufficient
for stability. It is not necessary: the product foliation of $L\times\mathbb R^q$
by the slices $L\times\{t\}$ has compact leaves with trivial holonomy for every
compact leaf $L$, including leaves with infinite fundamental group. In
particular, for a compact leaf the hypothesis "finite holonomy" is strictly
weaker than "finite fundamental group".
entry.strategy:
The image of a finite group under the homomorphism $\rho_x$ is finite, reducing the sufficient direction to local Reeb stability. For the non-necessity, compute the holonomy of a leaf of a product foliation: transversals are the fibres $\{y\}\times\mathbb R^q$, the holonomy of any leafwise loop is trivial because the leafwise transport is the identity of the transversal in product coordinates. The product foliation is the trivial case of the construction, and the class of examples with infinite $\pi_1(L)$ is realised by the companion counterexample. No choice beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: In a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation a compact leaf with finite fundamental group has trivial holonomy
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a
transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$
([[def-transversely-oriented-codimension-one-foliation]]) and let $L$ be a
compact leaf with finite fundamental group
([[def-based-loops-and-fundamental-group]]). Then the holonomy group of $L$ is
trivial, and consequently $L$ has a fundamental system of product foliated
neighbourhoods $L\times D$ and every leaf in such a neighbourhood is compact
and diffeomorphic to $L$.
entry.strategy:
A local transversal $T$ at $x\in L$ is one-dimensional, and a co-orientation of $F$ orients $T$; the holonomy representation therefore lands in the group of germs of orientation-preserving local diffeomorphisms of $(\mathbb R,0)$, $\operatorname{Diff}^+_0(\mathbb R,0)$. Since $\pi_1(L,x)$ is finite, its image $H$ is finite; by [[lem-germs-of-orientation-preserving-diffeomorphisms-of-the-line-at-zero-are-torsion-free]] every finite subgroup of $\operatorname{Diff}^+_0(\mathbb R,0)$ is trivial, so $H=\{1\}$. Triviality of holonomy then gives product foliated neighbourhoods by [[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]]. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: A compact holonomy-free codimension-one foliation is fibered over its leaf space
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a
codimension-one foliation of a nonempty closed connected smooth manifold $M$ and
suppose that every leaf of $F$ is compact with trivial holonomy and that there
is a closed smooth manifold $L$ with every leaf diffeomorphic to $L$. Then the
leaf space $X:=M/F$ with the quotient topology
([[def-quotient-topology]]) is a compact connected Hausdorff topological
one-manifold, hence homeomorphic to $S^1$
([[lem-a-compact-connected-one-dimensional-manifold-without-boundary-is-a-circle]]);
and the quotient map $q:M\to X$ is a locally trivial fibre bundle with fibre
$L$: every leaf $L_0=q^{-1}(p)$ has a saturated product neighbourhood
$U\cong L_0\times D$ with $q(U)=:V$ a coordinate interval and $q|_U$ the
projection $L_0\times V\to V$. Equivalently, $M$ is the total space of a
locally trivial fibre bundle over the circle whose fibres are the leaves of
$F$. Choosing a smooth transverse connection identifies the monodromy with the return diffeomorphism of the entire fibre $L_0$ after one circuit of $X$; its isotopy class is independent of that choice. The foliation is the fibre foliation of that bundle.
entry.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A codimension-one foliation $F$ of a closed connected smooth manifold $M$ all of whose leaves are compact with trivial holonomy and diffeomorphic to a fixed closed smooth manifold $L$.

[F1] A compact leaf with trivial (in particular finite) holonomy has a fundamental system of saturated product neighbourhoods $L_0\times D$, with $D$ an open interval, and every leaf in such a neighbourhood is compact and diffeomorphic to $L_0$ ([[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]], [[def-saturated-neighbourhood-of-a-leaf]]).

[F2] The leaf space $X=M/F$ is by definition the quotient of $M$ by the equivalence relation "same leaf", with the quotient topology; it is compact and connected when $M$ is, and it is Hausdorff when distinct leaves can be separated by saturated open sets ([[def-quotient-topology]], [[def-compact-space]], [[def-connected-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]).

[F3] A nonempty compact connected topological one-manifold without boundary is homeomorphic to $S^1$ ([[lem-a-compact-connected-one-dimensional-manifold-without-boundary-is-a-circle]]).

[F4] The product neighborhoods can be taken smooth, with smooth transverse coordinate changes ([[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]]).

[F5] Smooth partitions of unity patch local lifts, compact smooth vector fields are complete, and their local ODE flows depend smoothly on parameters ([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]], [[cor-every-smooth-vector-field-on-a-compact-manifold-is-complete]], [[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 (Leaf-space charts and local trivializations.) Let $L_0=q^{-1}(p)$ be a leaf. By [F1] it has a saturated product neighbourhood $U\cong L_0\times D$ with $D$ an open interval, and $U$ is a union of leaves, so $q(U)$ is an open subset of $X$ homeomorphic to $D$: the map $q|_U$ is the projection $L_0\times D\to D$ followed by the identification $q(U)\cong D$. These charts make $X$ locally Euclidean of dimension one, and the transition maps between two such charts are the transverse coordinate changes of the foliation, hence homeomorphisms. [F1, F2]

1.2 (Hausdorffness.) Let $p_1\neq p_2$ in $X$ correspond to distinct leaves $L_1\neq L_2$. These are disjoint compact subsets of the Hausdorff manifold $M$; choosing saturated product neighbourhoods as in [F1] inside disjoint open neighbourhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ gives disjoint open sets $q(U_1)\ni p_1$ and $q(U_2)\ni p_2$ in $X$, because a leaf meeting $U_i$ is contained in $U_i$. Hence $X$ is Hausdorff. [F1, F2]

2.1 (Compactness, connectedness, no boundary.) $X$ is compact and connected as a continuous image of $M$ [F2], and by step 1.1 every point of $X$ has a neighbourhood homeomorphic to an open interval, so $X$ has no boundary; by [F3] $X$ is homeomorphic to $S^1$. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 (Whole-fibre return.) The maps in step 1.1 are local trivializations with fibre $L_0\cong L$. By F4 their interval coordinate changes are smooth, so $X$ is a smooth circle. Choose a positive base vector field of period one, lift it in the finitely many product trivializations, and patch the lifts with a finite smooth partition of unity. The patched field still projects to the base field. Compactness of $M$ gives its flow for time one, and that flow restricts to a diffeomorphism of the whole fibre $L_0$ onto itself. Flow over $[0,1]$ trivializes the pullback bundle; the endpoint gluing is exactly this return map. Convex interpolation of two such lifts, followed by smooth flow dependence, proves that their return maps are isotopic. A closed transversal is a single curve and does not itself determine a whole-fibre return map. [F1, F4, F5, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Therefore the leaf space is a compact connected Hausdorff one-manifold homeomorphic to $S^1$ and $q:M\to X$ is a locally trivial fibre bundle with fibre $L$ whose monodromy is the whole-fibre return map for a chosen transverse connection, with the foliation as its fibre foliation. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

entry.title: Compact stable leaves form an open saturated set
entry.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a
transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a smooth manifold $M$, let
$L$ be a compact leaf with finite fundamental group
([[def-transversely-oriented-codimension-one-foliation]]), and let
$S\subseteq M$ be the union of the leaves of $F$ that are compact and
diffeomorphic to $L$. Then $S$ is open and saturated, and it is nonempty (it
contains $L$). More generally, for any regular foliation the union of the
compact leaves with finite holonomy group is open and saturated.
entry.strategy:
A union of leaves is saturated by definition. For openness: if $x\in S$ with leaf $L_x$, then $L_x$ is compact with $\pi_1(L_x)$ finite, so by [[lem-a-compact-codimension-one-leaf-with-finite-fundamental-group-has-trivial-holonomy-when-transversely-oriented]] its holonomy is trivial, and [[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]] supplies a saturated product neighbourhood $U\cong L_x\times D$ of $L_x$ all of whose leaves are compact and diffeomorphic to $L_x\cong L$; hence $U\subseteq S$. The general statement is the same argument with [[thm-local-reeb-stability]], whose conclusion gives a saturated neighbourhood all of whose leaves are compact with finite holonomy. Only the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: A compact leaf neither has finite holonomy nor finite fundamental group automatically
entry.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). The hypotheses
"compact leaf", "finite holonomy" and "finite fundamental group" are pairwise
distinct for compact leaves.

The boundary torus of the Reeb foliation of the solid torus
([[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]],
[[def-two-dimensional-torus]]) is compact but has infinite holonomy and
infinite fundamental group, and it is not stable, so compactness of the leaf
does not imply finiteness of the holonomy group. Conversely a leaf of a product
foliation $L\times S^1$ by the slices is compact with trivial holonomy for
every closed $L$, including $L=T^2$ with infinite fundamental group, so
finiteness of the holonomy is not necessary for compactness or stability, and
"finite holonomy" is strictly weaker than "finite fundamental group"
([[cor-finite-fundamental-group-is-a-sufficient-not-necessary-reeb-stability-hypothesis]]).
entry.strategy: The Reeb example is computed in [[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]]: the boundary leaf is compact, its holonomy contains a non-identity contraction germ and hence is infinite, and stability fails. The product example is the trivial-representation case of the suspension construction, where the holonomy of every leaf is trivial while $\pi_1(L)$ can be infinite. The two computations show that no implication between the three conditions holds in general and identify the exact hypothesis used by the local theorem. No proof obligation beyond these cited computations arises; the remark carries 'proof not applicable'.

entry.title: Closedness of the set of compact leaves in a transversely oriented codimension-one foliation
entry.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), which in particular supplies $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $F$ be a smooth transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed connected smooth manifold $M$. Suppose that $L$ is a compact leaf with finite fundamental group. The union $S$ of the compact leaves diffeomorphic to $L$ is closed. Since it is nonempty and open, $S=M$. Every leaf is therefore compact, diffeomorphic to $L$, and has trivial holonomy.
entry.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The foliation, ambient manifold, distinguished leaf and choice assumption of the statement; write $d=\dim M$.

[F1] $S$ is nonempty, open and saturated ([[lem-compact-stable-leaves-form-an-open-saturated-set]]).

[F2] Compact leaves are embedded hypersurfaces ([[lem-compact-c1-foliation-leaf-is-an-embedded-hypersurface]]); their fundamental groups are finitely generated ([[lem-compact-c1-leaf-has-finitely-generated-fundamental-group]]).

[F3] Holonomy is constructed by finite plaque transport and is invariant under leafwise homotopies; in the cooriented case it consists of increasing transverse maps ([[lem-c1-holonomy-is-a-well-defined-representation-into-transverse-germs]]).

[F4] In a closed oriented smooth $d$-manifold, a positive closed immersed transversal missing finitely many consistently oriented compact leaves but meeting another detects a homology class outside their rational span ([[lem-oriented-intersection-detects-nonvanishing-rational-homology]]).

[F5] Rational homology of a closed smooth manifold is finite dimensional under the declared full-AC hypothesis ([[lem-rational-homology-of-a-closed-smooth-manifold-is-finite-dimensional]]). The finite-CW input has the same hypothesis ([[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]).

[F6] The locally defined tangent-orientation double cover is smooth, oriented and finite-sheeted by [[lem-the-orientable-double-cover-of-a-smooth-manifold]].

[F7] A compact leaf with finite fundamental group has trivial holonomy in a cooriented codimension-one foliation ([[lem-a-compact-codimension-one-leaf-with-finite-fundamental-group-has-trivial-holonomy-when-transversely-oriented]]).

[F8] A smooth map with invertible differential is a local diffeomorphism ([[thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds]]).

## Proof

1.1 (A noncompact leaf and finite barriers.) Suppose first that $M$ is oriented and that $x\in\overline S$ lies on an intrinsically noncompact leaf $A$. Fix any finite collection $B_1,\ldots,B_k$ of leaves in $S$. Cover $M$ by finitely many smaller foliation boxes whose closures lie inside larger boxes. If $A$ met only finitely many plaques in every larger box, the closed plaque disks containing all its intersections with the smaller boxes would form a finite compact cover of $A$ in its intrinsic topology, a contradiction. Thus some box contains infinitely many distinct plaques of $A$ meeting its smaller box. Refine the boxes so that each $B_i$, being embedded compact, meets a box either in one slice or not at all; finitely many such refinements suffice. Two of the infinitely many $A$-plaques then lie in the same interval cut out by the finitely many barrier slices. Join their central points by a compact embedded leafwise arc in $A$, oriented from the higher plaque to the lower one. Its compact image misses every $B_i$. Finite plaque transports along that arc construct a thin foliated strip, with consistently positive transverse coordinate $u$ and central arc $u=0$. Tilt the arc from $u=-\varepsilon$ to $u=\varepsilon$ with strictly positive derivative. For sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ its final point still lies below its initial point in the original box; the positive vertical segment between them completes a closed positive immersed transversal $\gamma$. Both the strip and the vertical segment miss all barriers; the tilted arc crosses $A$ at $u=0$. Smooth the two corners inside boxes: the positive transverse half-space of tangent vectors is convex, so a sufficiently small smoothing preserves positivity and barrier avoidance. This is the compact-ambient version of the construction behind [[lem-a-non-closed-leaf-of-a-codimension-one-foliation-meets-a-closed-transversal]], proved here for intrinsic noncompactness without equating it with nonclosedness. [F2, F3, construct]

1.2 (Finite control near a compact reference leaf.) Let $A$ now be any compact cooriented leaf, with base point $a$ and a short transversal $T$ at $a$ carrying coordinate $t=0$ on $A$. A transverse collar projection onto $A$ exists: choose a positive transverse smooth vector field by finitely many local fields and chart bumps, and flow it for a common short time; its differential at time zero is invertible by F8, and compactness plus injectivity on the zero section makes it injective after shrinking. The pulled-back foliation is transverse to collar fibres. Choose finitely many generators of $\pi_1(A,a)$ by F2, and finitely many contractible coordinate disks with relatively compact smaller disks covering $A$. They may be chosen with contractible connected overlaps by taking sufficiently small strongly convex balls for a smooth metric on compact $A$; the local exponential inverse and positive Hessian of squared distance give such balls, and compactness supplies a finite subcover. Fix paths from $a$ to their centers and paths across their nonempty overlaps. The finite overlap comparison loops are words in the chosen generators. Fix the finitely many homotopies witnessing these words. Compactness of those paths, disks and homotopies gives a common interval on which their plaque transports and comparisons are defined, by a finite box subdivision. Denote the resulting increasing generator maps by $H_j$; include inverses in this finite list and shrink again so both directions are defined on an interval about zero. No assertion of uniform transport along all possible paths is used. [F2, F3, F8, construct]

2.1 (Finite homology excludes noncompact limits.) The saturation of $\gamma$ is open: in a box a short transverse segment has open plaque saturation, and transport along any finite leafwise path carries such an open interval to an open interval. It contains the entire leaf $A$, hence $x$. Since $x\in\overline S$, some leaf $B\subset S$ meets $\gamma$. Orient compact leaves by the ambient orientation and positive normal. By F4, $[B]$ is outside the span of $[B_1],\ldots,[B_k]$ in $H_{d-1}(M;\mathbb Q)$. But by F5 the span of the classes of ALL leaves in $S$ has a finite basis chosen from those classes: starting with the empty list, append an independent member while possible, at most $\dim H_{d-1}$ times. This is only a finite selection. Apply step 1.1 to the leaves representing that finite basis. The new class cannot lie outside their span, a contradiction. Thus the leaf through any point of $\overline S$ is compact. For $d=1$ all leaves are points already, so this argument is unnecessary. [F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 (Compactness forces every generator to fix the nearby parameter.) Take $|t|$ sufficiently small in the interval of step 1.2 and suppose its leaf $B$ is compact. If $t>0$ and $H_j(t)<t$, forward iterates of $H_j$ remain between zero and $t$, strictly decrease, and are distinct. If $H_j(t)>t$, use inverse iterates, which remain between zero and $t$ and strictly decrease. The chosen common domains contain this interval, so every iterate is defined and lies on $B\cap T$. If $t<0$, use forward or inverse iterates that strictly increase towards zero and remain between $t$ and zero. In all cases these give infinitely many distinct intersections in a compact subinterval of $T$. Since $B$ is embedded compact by F2, its intersection with that subinterval is closed and discrete (the transversal is transverse at every intersection), hence finite. This contradiction shows $H_j(t)=t$ for every generator. At $t=0$ this is automatic. [F2, step 1.2]

3.1 (The one-sheeted graph.) Continue the point $t$ over each coordinate disk using its fixed center path and radial plaque transports in the collar. Each continuation is a smooth graph over that disk, because projection is a local diffeomorphism on plaques. On an overlap, the two continuations differ by its comparison loop. The fixed homotopy of step 1.2 expresses that comparison as a word in generators, each fixing $t$ by step 2.2; all finite intermediate transports are defined after the common shrink. Homotopy invariance in F3 therefore identifies the two graphs. They patch to a single compact graph over all of $A$, contained in $B$. Its image is open in the intrinsic topology of $B$ by the local graph charts, and closed there because its compact domain maps into the Hausdorff leaf $B$. Connectedness of $B$ makes the image all of $B$. Thus collar projection restricts to a diffeomorphism $B\to A$. [F3, F8, step 1.2, step 2.2]

4.1 (Closedness in the oriented case.) For $x\in\overline S$, step 2.1 makes its leaf $A$ compact. Every sufficiently small neighborhood of $x$ meets $S$; inside the collar of step 1.2 project such a point along its plaque to the base transversal $T$. Its leaf $B\subset S$ is compact and has sufficiently small base parameter, so step 3.1 gives $A\cong B\cong L$. Hence $x\in S$. This proves $\overline S\subset S$, and therefore closedness. This uses neither a Hausdorff limit of leaf sets nor an assertion that a connected saturated limit is a single leaf. [F1, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 (Nonorientable ambient manifolds.) For nonorientable $M$ pass to its orientation double cover $p:\widetilde M\to M$ from F6. The local two-sheet construction is smooth, oriented, and compact: finitely many relatively compact evenly covered boxes cover the compact base, and their finitely many lifted closures cover the total space. Pull back the cooriented foliation. If the leaf $A$ through $x\in\overline S$ were intrinsically noncompact, each lifted leaf covering $A$ would be noncompact, since a compact lifted leaf would surject onto $A$. At a lift of $x$, the union of lifted leaves from $S$ accumulates; all these leaves are compact finite covers of leaves in $S$. The finite-barrier and homology arguments above apply to this entire collection in the oriented cover: the argument requires compact leaves and a finite-dimensional homology space, not a common diffeomorphism type. They exclude the presumed noncompact lifted leaf. Thus $A$ is compact downstairs. The compact-reference graph argument uses coorientation alone, so step 4.1 applies downstairs unchanged. [F2, F4, F5, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1]

6.1 In every case $S$ is closed, nonempty and open by F1. Connectedness gives $S=M$; each leaf is diffeomorphic to the finite-fundamental-group leaf $L$, so F7 gives trivial holonomy for every leaf. Full AC is retained precisely for F5 and the declared finite-CW chain; it is not replaced by countable choice. The finite barrier, graph and basis selections add no arbitrary-index choice. [F1, F7, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

entry.title: Global Reeb stability for transversely oriented codimension-one foliations
entry.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $F$ be a smooth transversely oriented codimension-one foliation of a closed connected smooth manifold $M$, and suppose some leaf $L$ is compact with finite fundamental group. Every leaf is compact, diffeomorphic to $L$, and has trivial holonomy. The leaf space $M/F$ is a circle, and the quotient is a smooth locally trivial fibre bundle $q:M\to S^1$ whose fibres are exactly the leaves. Its total space is a mapping torus of a diffeomorphism of $L$. A choice of transverse connection identifies its monodromy with the return diffeomorphism of the whole fibre after one circuit of the base; its isotopy class is independent of that choice.

The boundary/interval variant is a separate theorem. No boundary is allowed in the present statement.
entry.strategy:
Compactness is essential and enters through the limit argument. First, $\pi_1(L)$ finite and transverse orientability force the holonomy of $L$ to be trivial ([[lem-a-compact-codimension-one-leaf-with-finite-fundamental-group-has-trivial-holonomy-when-transversely-oriented]]). Let $S$ be the union of the leaves diffeomorphic to $L$; $S$ is open, saturated and nonempty ([[lem-compact-stable-leaves-form-an-open-saturated-set]]), and it is closed by the limit argument of [[lem-compact-leaf-control-and-compact-ambientness-give-the-required-closedness]], which uses the co-orientation, the existence of a closed transversal through a non-closed leaf, the intersection-detection lemma and finite-dimensionality of $H_{\dim M-1}(M;\mathbb Q)$. Since $M$ is connected, $S=M$: all leaves are compact and diffeomorphic to $L$, and the codimension-one trivial-holonomy lemma makes their holonomy trivial. The fibre-bundle-over-$S^1$ conclusion is then [[lem-a-compact-holonomy-free-codimension-one-foliation-is-a-fiber-bundle-over-its-leaf-space]]. Full AC is required by the cited finite-dimensional rational-homology and finite-CW suppliers in the closedness argument; it supplies the countable-choice principle by [[lem-axiom-of-choice-implies-countable-choice]] ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). All regularity hypotheses are smooth.

Here $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ denotes the countable-choice principle [[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]].

entry.title: A fibration over the circle as a globally stable foliation
entry.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $T^2=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ and $f(x,y)=(x+y,y)$. Its mapping torus, with quotient action $(z,t)\mapsto(f(z),t+1)$, has a smooth cooriented fibre foliation with compact torus leaves and trivial holonomy. Positive-time return is the inverse Dehn twist $f^{-1}(x,y)=(x-y,y)$. The bundle is not the product bundle over $S^1$. It illustrates the fibration conclusion of global Reeb stability; since torus fundamental groups are infinite, it does not satisfy that theorem's finite-fundamental-group hypothesis.
entry.strategy: Compute inverse and quotient return; invoke the mapping-torus supplier for leaves and holonomy; compute the nonidentity integral matrix on torus loops, obstructing isotopy to identity and hence product bundle triviality. No full AC theorem is applied.

entry.title: The finite-holonomy normal model of the Möbius band
entry.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let
$$M:=\bigl(S^1\times(-1,1)\bigr)/\mathbb Z_2$$
be the Möbius band, the quotient by the free involution
$\tau(u,v):=(u+\tfrac12,-v)$, foliated by the images of the circles
$S^1\times\{v\}$. The central leaf $L_0$ (image of $v=0$) is the circle
$\mathbb R/(\tfrac12\mathbb Z)$ whose holonomy group is $\mathbb Z_2$,
generated by the reflection germ $v\mapsto-v$ of a transversal interval: going
once around the central leaf identifies the transversal coordinate $v$ with
$-v$ ([[def-holonomy-representation-and-holonomy-group-of-a-leaf]]). Its
holonomy cover is the connected double cover
$\widehat L_0=S^1\to L_0$
([[def-holonomy-cover-of-a-leaf]]), the deck group is $\mathbb Z_2$ acting by
$u\mapsto u+\tfrac12$, and the finite-holonomy normal model
$(\widehat L_0\times D)/\mathbb Z_2$ with the diagonal action
$(u,v)\mapsto(u+\tfrac12,-v)$ is exactly the Möbius band with its foliation:
the quotient recovers the surface and the central leaf
$(\widehat L_0\times\{0\})/\mathbb Z_2\cong L_0$. The other leaves are images
of $S^1\times\{v\}$ and double-cover the central leaf, as predicted by the
finite-holonomy model.
entry.strategy: Verification: (1) the involution $(u,v)\mapsto(u+\tfrac12,-v)$ is free on $S^1\times(-1,1)$ (it has no fixed point: $v=-v$ would force $v=0$, and then $u=u+\tfrac12$ is impossible on $S^1$), so the quotient is a smooth surface, in fact the Möbius band, the total space of the unique non-trivial interval bundle over $S^1$; (2) the foliation of $S^1\times(-1,1)$ by the slices $S^1\times\{v\}$ is mapped to itself by the involution (up to the reflection $v\mapsto-v$), and [[prop-quotient-foliation-under-a-free-proper-foliated-action]] descends it; (3) the central leaf is $\mathbb R/(\tfrac12\mathbb Z)\cong S^1$, and following it once around (from $u$ to $u+\tfrac12$) returns the transversal coordinate $v$ to $-v$, so the return germ is the reflection $v\mapsto-v$ and the holonomy group is $\mathbb Z_2$; (4) the holonomy cover has deck group $\mathbb Z_2$ acting by $u\mapsto u+\tfrac12$ by [[lem-deck-group-of-the-holonomy-cover-is-the-holonomy-group]], so the normal model is the diagonal quotient $(\widehat L_0\times D)/\mathbb Z_2$, which is the Möbius band by the very definition of the quotient; (5) leaves other than the central one are the images of the slices $v\neq0$ and meet a small transversal in two points, i.e. double-cover $L_0$. The example therefore tests the normal model and the deck-group description. No choice beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

entry.title: A Reeb component has a compact boundary leaf with infinite holonomy
entry.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The Reeb foliation of the solid torus $X=\overline D^2\times S^1$ ([[prop-reeb-foliation-of-the-solid-torus-has-the-boundary-as-a-leaf]]) has a compact leaf, the boundary torus $\partial X\cong T^2$, whose holonomy group is infinite: the holonomy of the loop in the $S^1$-factor is represented by the non-identity contraction germ determined by $u(r')=u(r)+1$, $u(r)=\exp(1/(1-r^2))$. Hence the compact leaf does not have finite holonomy, the hypothesis of [[thm-local-reeb-stability]] cannot be dropped, and the leaf is not stable: near the boundary leaf the interior leaves are planes that accumulate on it, so no saturated neighbourhood of the boundary leaf consists of compact leaves. The example also shows that the failure is not a failure of compactness of the ambient foliated manifold but a failure of finiteness of holonomy.
entry.strategy: Counterexample verification: (1) the boundary torus is a leaf by construction; (2) the holonomy of its $S^1$-direction loop is computed in the cited proposition and is a non-identity contraction, so the holonomy group is infinite; (3) if the boundary leaf were stable, a saturated neighbourhood of it would consist of leaves diffeomorphic to it (compact), but every interior leaf is a plane accumulating on the boundary, contradiction; (4) therefore local Reeb stability genuinely needs finite holonomy, and the Reeb component is the standard boundary case. No choice beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

entry.title: The product foliation near a compact leaf with trivial holonomy
entry.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice-principle-for-foliation-pair]]). Let $L=S^1$ and
consider the product foliation of $M=S^1\times\mathbb R$ by the circles
$L_t=S^1\times\{t\}$. Each leaf is compact and has trivial holonomy: a local
transversal is a vertical interval $\{u\}\times(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ and
the holonomy of any leafwise loop is the identity. For every leaf $L_{t_0}$ and
every $\delta>0$ the open set
$U_\delta=S^1\times(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ is a saturated neighbourhood of
$L_{t_0}$ foliated-diffeomorphic to the product $S^1\times(-\delta,\delta)$
with the product foliation, so the conclusion of
[[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]] is realised
exactly. The same computation with $L=T^2$ gives compact leaves with infinite
fundamental group and trivial holonomy, showing that trivial holonomy does not
require finiteness of $\pi_1$.
entry.strategy: Verification: (1) the slices $S^1\times\{t\}$ are the maximal connected integral manifolds of the kernel of $dt$, so they are the leaves; (2) a leafwise loop lies in a slice and the plaque transport in product coordinates is the identity, so the holonomy representation is trivial; (3) $U_\delta$ is open, saturated (a union of slices) and is identified with the product foliation by the identity in product coordinates; (4) for $L=T^2$ the same argument applies and [[cor-fundamental-group-of-two-dimensional-torus]] gives infinite $\pi_1$ of the leaf. The example therefore tests the product corollary and the distinction between finite holonomy and finite fundamental group. No choice principle beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.

entry.title: A compact leaf with infinite fundamental group can still have trivial holonomy
entry.statement: Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M=T^2\times S^1$ with the product foliation by the tori $L_\theta=T^2\times\{\theta\}$. Every leaf $L_\theta$ is compact with $\pi_1(L_\theta)\cong\mathbb Z^2$ infinite ([[cor-fundamental-group-of-two-dimensional-torus]]), yet its holonomy group is trivial: a transversal is a vertical circle segment $\{p\}\times(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ and the leafwise transport in product coordinates is the identity. Hence the leaf is stable with a product foliated neighbourhood $T^2\times(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)$ ([[cor-trivial-holonomy-gives-a-product-foliated-neighbourhood]]), and finiteness of the fundamental group is not necessary for stability. Together with the Reeb component counterexample this pins the exact hypothesis of local Reeb stability to finiteness of the holonomy group.
entry.strategy: Counterexample verification: (1) the slices are the leaves of the product foliation; (2) $\pi_1(T^2)\cong\mathbb Z^2$ is infinite; (3) holonomy around any leafwise loop is the identity of the transversal because the foliation is a product; (4) the product neighbourhood is saturated and foliated as a product, so the leaf is stable. The example therefore separates 'finite fundamental group' from 'stable/trivial holonomy'. No choice beyond the standing $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used.
